newsitem.title: USA: Commercial buying boosts soyoil, soymeal lower.
newsitem.headline: Commercial buying boosts soyoil, soymeal lower.

text.p: Commercial buying pushed CBOT soyoil futures higher at midsession Thursday and soymeal futures were pulled lower with soybeans, traders said.
"Commercials are the only game in town in soyoil," said one floor source. "There's nothing for sale."
In early trade, Produce Grain, Term Commodities and Iowa Grain each bought 100 lots of August soyoil, floor traders said.
USDA Thursday reported U.S. net export sales of soyoil for the week ended June 19 were 30,100 tonnes, which was well above expectations for 1,000 to 3,000 tonnes.

However, the report showed a 28,400-tonne sale to China, which had been widely talked in the trade up to two weeks ago. The sale was characterized by U.S. exporters as a "special deal," and more Chinese purchases of U.S. soyoil are unlikely.
Concerns that a drop in world soymeal values will spark heavy defaults from China also helped keep soymeal futures on the defensive, traders said.

At 1120 CDT, July soyoil was 0.20 cent a lb higher at 22.66 cents, and other months were 0.15 to 0.22 cent up. July soymeal was down $3.40 per ton at 265.50, and other months were $1.20 to $2.10 lower.
